$comment: Machine twin of scripts/mac/local-brain/CAPABILITIES.md: what the Mac's local brain may run, may run only under conditions, must leave to a cloud model, and must never run. The Markdown tables are generated from this file by node scripts/check-local-brain-capabilities.mjs --write, and the same script gates both. Every path:line or path:from-to citation, in a row's source or in the prose of the Markdown, has an entry in anchors: text the gate asserts sits on the first cited line (and, for a range, the last cited line) of the checked-out head and on no other line of that file, so a line inserted or removed at or above the end of a cited range turns the gate red. measuredAt names the commit the cited lines were last re-read in full (a commit of the branch that added this file: after a squash landing it is gone from the history, and the anchors, not that commit, are what the gate checks). If this file and the tree disagree, the tree wins: raise a hand.

fieldMeanings.readOnly: Writes nothing git sees in the checkout and changes nothing on the remote. Updating .git refs, a temp dir outside the checkout, or a throwaway worktree the command removes itself does not count.
fieldMeanings.writesTree: Creates or modifies a path git sees in the checkout, including mutate-then-restore.
fieldMeanings.needsNetwork: Reaches GitHub, origin or a package registry. networkWrites: pushes, deletes, opens a PR or merges.
fieldMeanings.needsToken: Refuses, or is useless, without a GitHub credential or push rights. tokenOptional: uses one if present.
fieldMeanings.macOnly: Refuses off macOS, or works only on macOS by construction.
fieldMeanings.cloudModelNeeded: Needs Claude or Codex, or a Claude session, to run.
fieldMeanings.policy: allowed: run any cycle. own-worktree: run only in your own worktree. own-worktree-host-lock: also hold the host verification lock. owner-grant: run only after the owner grants it in a registry row (a remote write, or a seam only the owner can connect). cloud-model: your floor; it needs Claude or Codex, so wait for credits. forbidden: never.
fieldMeanings.exists: What the gate checks to prove the command exists: a package.json script, a tracked file, or an export of that file. The command text must name it. On a line of several programs (a chain, a pipe, a subshell, $( )) the first pnpm run X is the packageScript X (or starts with the packageScriptPrefix) and the first node, bash or sh P or ./P is the file P; every further script or file on the line exists too; a program the gate cannot check needs exists null and a note. An import or workflow row's command contains the file. null for git, GitHub, role and pattern rows.
fieldMeanings.selfTest: A command that must equal a step that preflight or the breadth lane lists, or a workflow run: line. null when no lane runs one.
fieldMeanings.source: path or path:line or path:from-to. The gate checks the path is tracked and, for a line citation, that the lines are inside the file and that the citation's anchors sit on its first and last line.
fieldMeanings.commandPatterns: forbidden rows only: JavaScript regular-expression sources (no flags) tested against a shell command line. A match means: do not run it.
fieldMeanings.pathPatterns: forbidden rows only: regular-expression sources tested against a repo-relative file path you would change. A match means: do not change it.
fieldMeanings.controls: forbidden rows only: for each target with patterns, mustMatch lines (each must match a pattern of that row) and mustNotMatch lines (none may match). Asserted on every gate run.
fieldMeanings.anchors: citation -> its anchors. path:line takes one text; path:from-to takes { first, last }. Each text is one line of 12 to 200 characters that appears on exactly one line of the file: the cited line for a single line and for first, the last cited line for last. Every path:line or path:from-to citation in a row's source or in the Markdown prose needs an entry, and an anchor that no citation uses is a problem.
